newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Five Indonesian opposition supporters convicted.
newsitem.headline: Five Indonesian opposition supporters convicted.

text.p: Five supporters of Megawati Sukarnoputri, the ousted Indonesian minority party head, have been jailed for breaking police lines during a protest march in June, the Kompas newspaper reported on Thursday.

The report said the Central Jakarta State Court sentenced Herman Susilo, Edy Suwito and Rajim to seven months in jail. Sutrisno was sentenced to six months and Fauzan Nanang Prasetya for five months and 17 days.
Prasetya was freed after the hearing as his sentence matched time already served, Kompas said.
The Jakarta Post daily quoted defence lawyers as saying all five men would appeal the convictions.

The men had been charged with riding their motorcycles through police lines after a protest march by some 5,000 Megawati supporters on June 20 was stopped by police and troops outside the Gambir railway station in central Jakarta.

The demonstrators had been trying to march to the Department of the Interior to protest against the government's support for a rebel congress of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) at which Megawati was ousted by a government-approved rival.

Last month, 115 Megawati supporters were convicted of failing to obey police orders to disperse on July 27 when they occupied PDI headquarters during an attack by party rivals who were backed by security forces.
The 115 supporters were sentenced to four months and three days jail and then released the same day because the time already served matched the sentence.
The attack on PDI headquarters sparked the worst rioting in Jakarta in more than 20 years. At least five people died, more than 100 vehicles were burnt and dozens of buildings destroyed or damaged.
